equity_bridge.note: Provisions for pensions and similar obligations, 2026-06-30 balance sheet (H1-2026 report). Taken gross of tax; partly offset by defined-benefit assets inside other receivables, so mildly conservative.

equity_bridge.item: Harbour Energy plc stake at market
equity_bridge.note: Non-integral equity-accounted; income sits in net income from shareholdings, outside EBITDA, so the asset goes in the bridge. Market value ~EUR967m at 2026-06-30 (H1-2026 note 6) vs carrying EUR1,134m.

equity_bridge.item: Wintershall Dea residual (non-integral equity-accounted) at book
equity_bridge.note: Non-integral equity-accounted investments EUR1,636m less Harbour carrying EUR1,134m. Dividends from it (EUR890m from equity-accounted investments in H1-2026) are outside the EBITDA build.

Integral equity-accounted investments rose EUR1,307m in H1-2026 'chiefly' from the Surventis stake (consideration EUR7,123m less EUR5.8bn cash). Its equity income is excluded from the margin paths (they are set on the operating segments), so it is valued once, here.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: terminal nominal growth; historical CAGRs are distorted by perimeter changes (Wintershall Dea/O&G deconsolidation, Coatings to discontinued ops) and the 2022 energy-price revenue spike
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (-0.3%) vs revenue 5yr (+0.2%) are close, but every series is perimeter-distorted: FY2022 revenue EUR87.3bn was inflated by energy pass-through, FY2017 includes oil & gas, FY2025 excludes Coatings. EPS CAGRs are not computable (FY2020 and FY2022 EPS negative on impairments of Wintershall Dea/Nord Stream).
historical_growth.notes: SBC is zero (cash-settled LTI), so the owner-FCF series equals reported FCF (OCF less capex, after interest paid) - no SBC divergence. FCF fell from EUR4.8bn (FY2017) to EUR0.7bn (FY2024) as the Zhanjiang capex supercycle (capex 7.8-9.5% of sales FY2023-24) coincided with the chemical down-cycle; FY2025 recovered to EUR1.3bn.

scenario_narratives.base: BASF delivers the raised FY2026 guidance (EBITDA before special items EUR6.9-7.7bn, midpoint EUR7.3bn) on a +4.5% sales year helped by $80 Brent pass-through and the Zhanjiang start-up, then recovers only part of the way to its 2028 ambition. Chemicals and Nutrition & Care lead (Zhanjiang ramp, Nutrition & Health recovery after the 2024 isophytol fire), but the CEO's own warning that Zhanjiang returns are 'significantly lower than anticipated' and an 'overserved' Chinese market hold the reported EBITDA margin to ~13% (about 13.8% before special items, ~EUR9bn on ~EUR68bn sales by FY2031) - the bottom of the EUR9-11bn 2028 target range, reached three years late. Restructuring special items keep recurring at ~0.6-0.9pp of sales, as they have every year since 2019. Capex follows the EUR13bn 2026-29 plan, then normalises above D&A. Owner FCF settles around EUR3.0-3.6bn.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 'Winning Ways' self-help plus a cyclical upturn land the 2028 targets on time: EBITDA before special items ~EUR10bn (14.5% reported) as Zhanjiang reaches full run-rate into a China market whose capacity discipline improves, European cost programmes and plant closures restore Ludwigshafen competitiveness, and Materials/Industrial Solutions volumes recover with automotive and construction. Capex stays under the EUR13bn plan, ROCE approaches the ~10% target, and the portfolio simplification (Coatings done, Agricultural Solutions IPO by mid-2027, silicates sold) sharpens capital allocation. Growth runs at 3-5% for five years on volume plus price.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY2023-25 trough proves structural. Chinese chemical capacity keeps a lid on upstream spreads (sector profits already fell two years running), Zhanjiang earns below its cost of capital, and European energy, EU ETS and US tariff pressure leave Ludwigshafen permanently disadvantaged. The H1-2026 strength (partly a Strait of Hormuz/oil-price effect) unwinds in 2027; reported EBITDA margin sits at 10-10.5%, the 2028 targets are abandoned, and capex has to rise back to ~6% of sales for decarbonisation and ETS compliance. Sales growth runs at 1-2% as automotive and construction stay weak.

valuation_philosophy.summary: BASF is valued as a capital-intensive cyclical on an owner-FCF basis: unlevered free cash flow after lease cash, ~5-6% of sales capex and a working-capital drag on growth, discounted at a EUR 7.5% WACC with the terminal value capped at 15x FCF (12x in the bear) because the business is cyclical. The key finding is conversion: at a mid-cycle ~13% reported EBITDA margin, capex, lease, tax and working capital leave only ~30-35% of EBITDA as owner FCF, so the current price embeds delivery of the 2028 targets rather than the mid-cycle average. SBC is zero (cash-settled LTI), so the house and street bases coincide and band_position is null.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin cycle: management sizes the chemicals margin sensitivity at more than EUR1bn of EBITDA; each 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is worth several euros per share.
Zhanjiang (~EUR8.7bn) returns into an oversupplied Chinese market - the swing factor for the 2028 targets.
Recurring 'special items': the model treats ~0.6-0.9pp of sales as a permanent cost; if restructuring genuinely ends, the reported margin path is too low.
Agricultural Solutions IPO: a minority listing would add NCI and cash; a premium valuation could crystallise more than the consolidated DCF credits.
Equity-accounted stakes (Surventis 40%, Harbour, Wintershall Dea) are valued at book/market in the bridge; Surventis is LBO-levered, so its value is volatile.
Capex discipline: the EUR13bn 2026-29 plan sits below D&A; a return to growth capex or ETS-driven decarbonisation spend would cut FCF.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (BAS.DE, XETRA, EUR) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 41.48-55.05.
data_sources.financials: BAS.DE_Metrics.csv (FY2017-FY2025, H1-2026); BASF Report 2025 (IAS 7 lease reconciliation, net debt, D&A, buybacks); BASF Half-Year Financial Report 2026 (balance sheet 2026-06-30, cash-flow statement, net debt EUR17,117m, treasury shares, Coatings disposal note, equity-accounted investments note 6, adjusted FY2026 outlook).
data_sources.qualitative: BAS.DE_Analysis.json (segments, guidance, bull/bear, risks, recent developments incl. Coatings sale, Agricultural Solutions IPO, Zhanjiang).

inputs.share_count_basis: Shares outstanding at 2026-06-30: 892,522,164 issued less 31,600,261 treasury shares (H1-2026 report note 7, lines 2749-2752) = 860.92m. No dilutive securities: BASF's long-term incentive is cash-settled, so basic = diluted. Held FLAT. The EUR1.5bn programme (Nov-2025 to Jun-2026) is complete; further buybacks under the >=EUR4bn 2025-2028 commitment would shrink the count but are a use of the FCF already valued, so they are not modelled as accretion.
inputs.sbc_source: No equity-settled share-based payment: BASF's LTI programme is cash-settled and expensed inside EBITDA; the cash-flow statement carries no SBC add-back (FY2025 Annual, H1-2026 cash-flow statement). SBC-zero market.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:38:34Z (XETRA close, Friday; Yahoo chart API regularMarketTime)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in EUR, the currency of the flows. Risk-free 2.7% (10y Bund), ERP 5.5%, levered beta 1.1 -> cost of equity ~8.8%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~3.6% (A-/A3, EUR bond curve) -> ~2.7% after tax. Market weights ~73% equity (EUR45bn cap) / 27% net debt + pensions -> ~7.1%; rounded up to 7.5% as the house rate for a European cyclical. Same WACC in every scenario: cyclicality and China overcapacity are charged in the scenario flows, not stacked on the discount rate (adaptations 7f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease cash (FY2025 principal EUR432m per IAS 7 reconciliation, plus ~EUR50m lease interest) ~0.8% of sales deducted via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (EUR1,608m at FY2025) are EXCLUDED from net debt, which matches BASF's own net-debt definition (financial indebtedness less cash and marketable securities; leases are a separate IAS 7 line). D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%); NCI deducted once in the equity bridge at book value (EUR1,077m, 2026-06-30). NCI is small (~2-3% of net income; H1-2026 continuing NCI EUR28m), so book is an adequate proxy. A future Agricultural Solutions IPO of a minority stake would create a large new NCI offset by cash; not modelled.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, plus the non-US/cyclical adaptations (EUR WACC, lease treatment B, NCI in bridge, non-operating equity stakes in bridge, SBC-zero). Routed per dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'. BASF is an integrated chemicals operating company - not a bank/REIT/holdco - and its value is a free-cash-flow stream. No prior BAS.DE valuation or MEMORY entry exists; this is a fresh build. PERIMETER: FY0 is FY2025 continuing operations ex-Coatings (sales EUR59,657m; EBITDA before special items EUR6,554m = 11.0%; reported EBITDA EUR5,618m). The Coatings sale to Carlyle closed 2026-06-30 (EUR5.8bn pre-tax cash, 40% Surventis stake retained); H1-2026 net income of EUR5,072m includes the EUR3,507m after-tax disposal gain and is NOT used as run-rate. MARGIN BASIS: ebitda_margin_path is REPORTED EBITDA, i.e. EBITDA before special items less a recurring ~0.6-0.9pp of restructuring 'special items' that BASF has booked every year 2019-2026 (H1-2026 -EUR654m; FY2025 -EUR936m). FY2026 base 10.8% = guidance midpoint EUR7.3bn bsi (raised at H1 from EUR6.2-7.0bn to EUR6.9-7.7bn) less ~EUR0.6bn specials on ~EUR62bn sales. Mid-cycle anchor: ex-O&G EBITDA bsi margin averaged ~14% over FY2018-FY2022 and ~11-12% over the FY2023-FY2025 trough. CAPEX: FY2026 guided ~EUR3.3bn and EUR13.0bn cumulative 2026-2029 (~5.1-5.3% of sales, below D&A) after the Zhanjiang build; then normalises to ~5.8% (above ex-ROU D&A of ~5.5%, consistent with 2% growth). WORKING CAPITAL: trade receivables + inventories less payables ~31% of sales, so growth consumes cash (wc_capture -20% of the revenue change). INTEREST INCOME: not stripped - BASF is in net debt (EUR17.1bn), so the matching-asset rule does not bite on cash. BUYBACKS: EUR355m in Q4-2025 and EUR1,145m in H1-2026 (EUR1.5bn programme complete); BASF is a funded repurchaser. Q3-2026 results are not yet published at valuation date (due late October); the next update should re-judge the FY2026 year only.

bear.narrative: Trough becomes the norm: China overcapacity caps upstream spreads, Ludwigshafen stays uncompetitive on energy/ETS, margin stuck near FY2023-25 levels.

base.narrative: Guidance-midpoint FY2026, then a partial cyclical recovery to a ~13% reported (~13.8% before special items) EBITDA margin by FY2031 - roughly the ex-O&G mid-cycle average, but short of the 2028 target.

bull.narrative: 2028 targets delivered: EBITDA before special items ~EUR10bn (14.5% reported + specials) on a fully-run Zhanjiang Verbund, capex held to the EUR13bn 2026-29 plan.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: China overcapacity and Europe's energy-cost gap are management's own top-rated risks, and BASF missed its outlook and consensus in FY2025. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things at once - a cyclical upturn, China capacity discipline, Zhanjiang at target returns and European self-help - and BASF has trailed its medium-term glide path since 2023. Base at 50%: the raised FY2026 guidance and A-rated balance sheet make the midpoint-then-partial-recovery path the central case. No solvency tail (A-/A3/A ratings, net debt EUR17.1bn and falling).
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
